reviewer_notes: BLT v1 §2.3 estimates conditional next-byte distribution entropy using a separately trained byte LM; global and relative-threshold rules set cuts. §2.4 requires incremental, future-independent patching. §4.2–4.4 specify the entropy model and chosen average patch-size thresholds. No joint LM-loss training of the threshold rule is implied.

BLT v1 §3.1–3.3: expensive global model works at patch resolution; local byte encoder forms patch features via pooling/cross-attention; local decoder also receives encoder byte representations. A patch vocabulary is not required, even though byte and optional n-gram embeddings still exist.

H-Net v2 §2.1 equation (3) retains an encoder-to-decoder residual; both outer networks work on uncompressed positions. §2.2 equation (4) computes boundary scores from current and previous encoder outputs, threshold 0.5, with boundary-vector selection. Equations (5)–(9) use smoothing and STE for learning signals. Equation (10) and the combined autoregressive + ratio loss guide the target compression ratio rather than enforce exact per-example lengths.

H-Net v2 §2.4 preserves causality and updates only states while generating bytes; fixed trained weights can still select different positions for different inputs. §4 Efficiency explicitly discusses engineering overhead; no wall-clock gain is deduced from counts.

BLT §2.4 describes fixed-vocabulary BPE and non-incremental prefix cuts. H-Net Appendix A.1 distinguishes isotropic/static/external/dynamic chunking; variable length by itself is insufficient to establish an end-to-end learned route.

Unicode 17 §3.9 D79 and D92 define character-encoding mappings, not language-model token vocabularies. Table 3-7 maps the ASCII code-point range to one-byte UTF-8; nothing in these definitions requires a learned subword tokenizer.
